newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Packer casino pullout fuels Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: Packer casino pullout fuels Fairfax.

text.p: Shares in Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd slipped three cents or 1.4 percent to A$2.13 on Monday after Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd withdrew a A$240 million deal to buy the casino's management contract.

The withdrawal, announced on the weekend, provided fuel for ongoing speculation that Publishing and Broadcasting was preparing itself for a tilt at newspaper publisher, John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, once the Federal government modified cross-media laws.
Fairfax shares added seven cents to A$3.30, equalling their three-year high reached on May 1.

"That's obviously the direction he is going to take," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage, noting that while any move would require changes in the law, such changes were already likely afoot if recent market speculation proved well-founded.

PBL had an option to buy 85 percent of the Sydney casino's management contract from U.S. based Showboat Inc. PBL also said it would not proceed with an option to buy a 10 percent stake in the casino's owner, Sydney Harbour Casino.
PBL said it had allowed the deal to lapse because of difficulties encountered with the Casino Control Authority (CCA), the regulator of casinos in New South Wales.
By 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), Fairfax shares were six cents higher at A$3.29 on turnover of 438,244 shares, while Sydney Harbour Casino shares were three cents lower at A$2.13 with 521,793 shares traded.
PBL shares were four cents down at A$6.66 on turnover of 153,533 shares.
